judge_reasoning: The model solution follows the same core line as the official solution: cast Quarry Hauler to push Kiora to 8 loyalty, use -8 to create three Octopi and the fight emblem, use two Octopi to kill one Colossus, sacrifice the third Octopus fight against Festering Mummy to trigger its death ability, which triggers Hapatra to make a deathtouch Snake, which kills the second Colossus via the emblem trigger, clearing the way for lethal combat damage with Hapatra and Weaver of Currents. The only difference is the target of Festering Mummy's -1/-1 counter (placed on the remaining Colossus rather than an unrelated permanent), which is inconsequential since Hapatra's trigger fires regardless of target, and the deathtouch fight kills the Colossus regardless of its toughness. Mana, timing, and legality checks all hold up.
model_solution:
1. Tap both Forests and both Fetid Pools for {G}{G}{U/B}{U/B} and cast Quarry Hauler ({3}{G}). Do NOT tap Weaver of Currents for mana – it needs to stay untapped to attack.
2. Quarry Hauler's ETB targets Kiora, Master of the Depths: the only kind of counter on her is loyalty, so put another loyalty counter on her. Kiora goes to 8 loyalty. (No loyalty ability has been activated yet this turn, so −8 is still available.)
3. Activate Kiora's −8: get the emblem "Whenever a creature you control enters, you may have it fight target creature," then create three 8/8 Octopus tokens. All three Octopuses enter and trigger the emblem:
   - Octopus A fights Metalwork Colossus #1 (8 damage).
   - Octopus B fights Metalwork Colossus #1 (8 more damage = 16 ≥ 10 toughness; Colossus #1 dies).
   - Octopus C fights our own Festering Mummy: Mummy takes 8 and dies.
4. Festering Mummy's death trigger: put a -1/-1 counter on Metalwork Colossus #2 (now 9/9). Hapatra triggers ("whenever you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature") and creates a 1/1 green Snake with deathtouch.
5. The Snake enters → emblem triggers → the Snake fights Metalwork Colossus #2. The Snake deals 1 deathtouch damage to Colossus #2, which is destroyed as a state-based action (rule 702.2b).
   - The opponent can never use the Colossus graveyard ability: when Colossus #1 hits the graveyard they control only one artifact (Colossus #2), and after Colossus #2 dies they control none, so "Sacrifice two artifacts" can't be paid.
6. Go to combat and attack with Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons (2/2) and Weaver of Currents (2/2). The opponent has no creatures left to block and no other permanents or cards.
7. 4 combat damage is dealt to the opponent, who is at 4 life → opponent goes to 0 and loses.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the board state: opponent at 4 life with two 10/10 Metalwork Colossus blockers, while I have Festering Mummy, Hapatra, and Weaver of Currents plus Kiora at 7 loyalty. I'm working through my available mana from the Fetid Pools, Forests, and Weaver's tap ability, considering how Kiora's +1 could untap Weaver and a land for extra mana.

Since Splendid Agony puts -1/-1 counters on creatures and triggers Hapatra separately per creature, I'm noting that two counters split across two targets would make two deathtouch snakes, but they'd have summoning sickness and couldn't attack this turn — so I need another way to push through 4 damage against two potential blockers with my combined 5 power of attackers.

Committing a Colossus back into their library removes one blocker for 3U, leaving just one 10/10 up. I'm also weighing Mockery of Nature's emerge cost, sacrificing a creature to reduce it and potentially destroy an artifact, to try to clear both blockers before combat.

If I sacrifice Weaver to emerge Mockery for {4}{G} and destroy one Colossus, the opponent would only have one artifact left afterward, not enough to activate the recursion ability. Combined with Commit for 3U, that's 9 total mana, which I can hit if I tap Weaver, use Kiora to untap it plus a land, and work through the sequence carefully.

That covers Commit and Mockery's emerge cost with mana to spare, satisfying both U and G. But sacrificing Weaver for emerge and swinging with just Mummy and Hapatra only deals 3 damage, not enough to close out an opponent at 4 life — Hapatra's -1/-1 trigger happens after combat damage anyway, so the snake token wouldn't help this turn, and any snakes made would be summoning sick regardless. I need to find another angle.

Attacking with all three creatures for 5 would be lethal, but that requires clearing both Colossi first, which costs too much mana through Mockery alone. Casting Quarry Hauler and using its counter-manipulation ability on Kiora's loyalty is another possible line, but the mana cost stacks up too high when combined with Commit.

Let me consider the emblem route instead — it grants fight triggers whenever a creature enters, so the three 8/8 Octopus tokens would each get to fight a target creature as they arrive, potentially clearing both Colossi through combined damage even though the Colossi would deal damage back and kill some Octopuses in the process.

Counting mana again, I'm short one for Splendid Agony after paying for Hauler with the forests and colorless. Kiora isn't a valid target since she's not a creature, so I'm reconsidering just going with fights instead: Octopus A fighting one of the Colossi to whittle it down.

Actually skipping Hauler and using Kiora's +1 instead won't reach 8 loyalty for the -8 ability this turn, so Hauler seems necessary. Let me check Mockery of Nature's cast trigger to destroy Colossus 1, emerging by sacrificing Weaver after tapping it for mana—that uses most of my mana but leaves Colossus 2 as a blocker with Mummy and Hapatra able to attack.

Going back to the Octopus plan: with 6 mana I can cast Hauler, then use Kiora's -8 for the emblem and three Octopuses. Two Octopuses can fight and kill Colossus 1, while the third deals 8 damage to Colossus 2. I'm checking whether Weaver can stay untapped by paying for Hauler with just the lands, letting Weaver join Mummy and Hapatra in the attack for 5 total power, with Colossus 2 only able to block one of them.

If Colossus 2 blocks Hapatra, 3 damage gets through — not enough. If it blocks Mummy, Mummy's death triggers a -1/-1 counter that creates a snake token, and Hapatra plus Weaver deal 4 damage, which is lethal. If it blocks Weaver, only 3 gets through. So the plan only works if Colossus 2 blocks Mummy specifically, meaning I need another way to remove Colossus 2 before combat, or reconsider the sequencing since Kiora's -8 requires Hauler to already be on board to reach 8 loyalty.

Thinking through mana allocation for casting Hauler and what's left over — after paying for Hauler, the remaining mana from Fetid Pools isn't enough to cast anything else useful, and cycling doesn't help either. After the ultimate resolves, I'm working out how to assign the octopus fight triggers against the two Colossus creatures to clear blockers.

Since both Colossi have counters on them but survive if only one hits each, I need to double up on one to actually kill it. Then I'm checking the attack step — the octopuses have summoning sickness so only Mummy, Hapatra, and Weaver can swing, and even if Colossus blocks and trades damage, it doesn't die outright from combat math. I'm also considering what happens if Festering Mummy dies and triggers its counter ability onto a target creature.

I realize I can use the emblem to have an octopus fight Festering Mummy directly, killing it and triggering its death ability to place a -1/-1 counter, which triggers Hapatra to make a snake, and that snake can then fight the weakened Colossus with deathtouch to finish it off. So the plan is: two octopuses fight Colossus 1 to kill it outright, while the third octopus fights Mummy, chaining into the snake token that deathtouches down Colossus 2. Now I'm checking what happens in the graveyard once Colossus 1 dies, since it might have a relevant ability there.

Colossus's return-from-graveyard ability needs two artifacts on the battlefield, but the opponent will only have one Colossus left once the first dies, so they can't activate it — and once both die, they'll have zero artifacts anyway, so there's no way for them to bring anything back. I don't think the opponent has any way to respond since they're tapped out with no cards in hand, and even sacrificing both Colossi to trigger something wouldn't give them enough artifacts to work with.

With that cleared up, I can attack with Hapatra and Weaver, both untapped 2/2s, for exactly 4 damage — lethal since the opponent has no blockers left and is at 4 life. Hauler and the Octopus tokens are summoning sick so they can't join the attack, but I don't need them. I'll pay for Hauler using two Forests plus two Fetid Pools rather than tapping Weaver, keeping it free to swing.

When fought by Octopus, Mummy dies from the damage and its death trigger puts a -1/-1 counter on Colossus 2 for safety, which also triggers Hapatra to make another snake. Then I move to combat, attacking with Hapatra and Weaver.

2711:606.3. A player may activate a loyalty ability of a permanent they control any time they have priority and the stack is empty during a main phase of their turn, but only if no player has previously activated a loyalty ability of that permanent that turn.
3355:701.12a A spell or ability may instruct players to exchange something (for example, life totals or control of two permanents) as part of its resolution. When such a spell or ability resolves, if the entire exchange can’t be completed, no part of the exchange occurs.
3358:701.12b When control of two permanents is exchanged, if those permanents are controlled by different players, each of those players simultaneously gains control of the permanent that was controlled by the other player. If, on the other hand, those permanents are controlled by the same player, the exchange effect does nothing.
3360:701.12c When life totals are exchanged, each player gains or loses the amount of life necessary to equal the other player’s previous life total. Replacement effects may modify these gains and losses, and triggered abilities may trigger on them. A player who can’t gain life can’t be given a higher life total this way, and a player who can’t lose life can’t be given a lower life total this way (see rules 119.7–8).
3881:702.2b A creature with toughness greater than 0 that’s been dealt damage by a source with deathtouch since the last time state-based actions were checked is destroyed as a state-based action. See rule 704.
